title_eng: Investigation of the Photoplethysmography Waveform according to the Nociceptive Pain
title_kor: Investigation of the Photoplethysmography Waveform according to the Nociceptive Pain
abstract:
Abstract— The purpose of this study was to examine some of 
features of the PPG waveform related to the surgical pain. 
Several parameters were combined with p ulse area, pulse 
amplitude, systolic, diastolic duration and pulse to pulse interval 
of PPG waveform and validated before and after the surgery. As 
a result, significant differences were found in parameters related 
to systolic duration (P<0.01) and diastolic duration (P<0.001) 
according to the surgical pain. 
I. INTRODUCTION 
For quantification of nociceptive pain, there have been 
many attempts to analyze the photoplethysmography (PPG) 
waveform reflecting the blood volume changes in the vessel 
affected by response of autonomic nervous system caused by 
pain stimuli [1-3]. In this research, we analyzed PPG 
waveform and investigated parameters that significantly 
affected by the surgical pain. 
II. MATERIALS AND METHODS 
Sixty surgical patients (29 males, 31 females, 52.1 ± 11.4 
years old) were enrolled to the experiment, and 58 pair of 
dataset was used except 2 pair of dataset which has recording 
error. According to the protocol, PPG data was recorded 
before and after surgery, and we regarded dataset recorded 
before surgery as a painless dataset and the rest as a pain 
dataset. Every record has 6-minute length and was recorded 
with 300 Hz sampling rate. To calculate the area of PPG 
waveform, every upper and lower peak location of the PPG 
waveform was detected and validated by proficient researchers. 
We calculated 6-values from PPG waveform as shown in 
Fig.1. Fig.1-①is the whole area under a pulse of PPG 
waveform (Area), Fig.1-② is the height from baseline to 
systolic peak (hsystole), Fig.1-③ is time interval between 
systolic peaks (PPIsystole), Fig.1-④ is time interval between 
diastolic peaks (PPIdiastole), Fig.1-⑤ is time interval between 
diastolic peak and systolic peak (Tsystole), and Fig.1-⑥ is time 
interval between systolic peak and next diastolic peak 
(Tdiastole). Because amplitude of PPG waveform is an arbitrary 
value, we divide area with pulse height ( hsystole) for 
normalization (Areanorm). 
Finally, we derived 5 parameters; Areanorm/hsystole, Areanorm 
/PPIsystole, Areanorm/PPIdiastole, Areanorm/Tsystole and Areanorm/ 
Tdiastole. Every parameter was derived in pain and painless 
dataset, and it was verified whether there is significant 
different using paired t-test or Wilcoxon signed rank test 
according to the data normality.

Finally, we derived 5 parameters; Areanorm/hsystole, Areanorm 
/PPIsystole, Areanorm/PPIdiastole, Areanorm/Tsystole and Areanorm/

dataset, and it was verified whether there is significant

according to the data normality. 
III. RESULTS AND DISCUSSIONS 
Fig. 2 shows that the fractional changes and significance 
of difference of the result of pulse area analysis according to 
the nociceptive pain. As a result, statistical difference was not 
found in Areanorm, Areanorm/PPIdiastole and Areanorm/PPIsystole 
but found in Areanorm/Tdiastole (P<0.001), Areanorm/Tsystole 
(P<0.01). This result is thought to be due to reduction of Tsystole 
and decrease of Tdiastole, considering the fact that Areanorm does 
not show any significant change with pain. 
IV. CONCLUSION 
The result of this study suggests that PPG waveform 
analysis is a promising approach for quantification of surgical 
pain. In this study, we only dealt with the existence of pain, 
however, the parameters derived from such studies are 
expected to be used for pain quantification in the future.
